correctness.rationale: Checked all alpha>=0 in the maximal diagonal domain. Since u=(1/j) in ell^2 and E=e_1 tensor u has E^2=E, T=(I+E)D is densely defined, closed, onto and has compact inverse D^-1(I-E/2). For S_alpha=R^alpha T the algebraic identity on D(D) is D_alpha x+e_1 sum_j x_j with D_alpha=diag(j^(1-alpha)). For alpha<1/2 the sum functional is bounded in the D_alpha graph norm because v_alpha=(j^(alpha-1)) lies in ell^2, giving the asserted closed (I+e_1 tensor v_alpha)D_alpha, with finite support a core. For alpha>=1/2, divergence of every tail sum of (1+j^(2(1-alpha)))^-1 yields tail vectors of arbitrarily small graph norm and prescribed sum, establishing exactly graph(D_alpha)+({0}×Ce_1), no larger multivalued part; the finite-dimensional vertical sum of a closed graph is closed. Projecting onto e_1 perpendicular gives q_reg and the singular first-coordinate form, by canonical form decomposition. Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz derives the exact finite N variational cost, and harmonic/summable series give the five asymptotic regimes including (log N)^-1/2 at alpha=1/2 and sqrt(2/N) at alpha=1. Verified independently finite-rank cost and boundary powers; finite tests do not prove the infinite threshold.
